subject: Runtime: KV cache compaction — priority, success metrics, staged rollout (runtime-1.22)
content:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 8:12 AM PST
Subject: Runtime: KV cache compaction — priority, success metrics, staged rollout (runtime-1.22)

Sean, Nikhil — looping you both in to align on priority + rollout expectations for KV cache compaction/eviction. We’re seeing enough evidence that fragmentation is a material contributor to burst-driven p95/p99 spikes (and occasional OOM/request shedding) on sustained decode with mixed sequence lengths.

I want to lock the following today so Omar/Samir/Sofia can execute without churn:

1) Priority / scope: this is a runtime-1.22 target and should be treated as P0 for Hosted tail latency stability. (Dedicated gets it behind a flag first.)

2) Success metrics (what we will hold canary to):
- Fragmentation ratio: reduce steady-state fragmentation under churn by >= 30% vs baseline on the mixed-length burst scenario.
- Tail latency: no regression; goal is p99 improvement during bursts. For gating I propose: p99 decode latency <= 1.10x baseline (5 min rolling) and <= 1.20x baseline (15 min rolling) for canary.
- OOM / request shedding: no increase (obviously) and ideally a measurable decrease in allocator-related failures.
- Compaction overhead: bounded; compaction time budgeted and visible.

3) Rollout sequencing:
- Stage 0: internal perf canary + staging load test.
- Stage 1: Hosted canary cohort (1% traffic) w/ automated rollback guardrails.
- Stage 2: Hosted expansion (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) if stable.
- Stage 3: Dedicated pools opt-in (flag + per-pool defaults), then broader.

Can you both reply with (a) the SRE guardrails you want for automated rollback / who can flip kill-switch, and (b) any product constraints / customer comms constraints on the above?

Design + tracking:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SERVE/KV+cache+compaction+improvements+(Design+Doc)
- Linear epic: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/kv-cache-compaction-epic

Thanks,
Mateo

—
Mateo Alvarez
VP Runtime, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 9:31 AM PST
Subject: Re: Runtime: KV cache compaction — priority, success metrics, staged rollout (runtime-1.22)

Agree this is the right priority.

SRE asks / rollout guardrails (Hoster canary):

Automated rollback criteria (per region, per model family where possible):
- p99 end-to-end latency (chat/generation routes): > 1.20x baseline for 10 min OR > 1.35x baseline for 3 min.
- Error rate: +0.30% absolute increase sustained 5 min (timeout/cancel/OOM buckets split out).
- GPU OOM events: any statistically meaningful increase vs baseline (we can start with “>= 2 events in 10 min” for canary nodes, but prefer to tune after first day).
- Compaction budget overrun signal: compaction_time_ms p95 > 2x configured budget for 10 min OR compaction_bytes_moved spikes correlate with queueing.

Kill-switch authority:
- Oncall SRE has authority to disable immediately for Hosted (feature flag), no approval needed.
- Notify runtime-oncall in #eng-oncall and leave a short note in the incident channel if triggered.

Also: please make sure the kill-switch is “fast” (config propagation within a couple minutes), and that disable semantics stop additional relocation work quickly (don’t keep a background worker copying for another 10+ minutes).

We’ll capture this in the guardrail doc and wire the alert routes. If you already have a metrics standard draft, send it over.

Hosted API tail latency guardrails doc (existing skeleton):
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Hosted+API+tail+latency+guardrails

— Sean

Sean Gallagher
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Runtime: KV cache compaction — priority, success metrics, staged rollout (runtime-1.22)

+1 on P0 and staging/Hosted-first.

Product constraints / messaging:
- For Hosted, we should assume this will be “silent” (no customer-facing knobs). If it improves p99, great; if it’s neutral, still fine — but we can’t accept regressions in stable (non-burst) traffic.
- For Dedicated, we need a crisp default posture: opt-in during first 2-3 weeks unless the Hosted rollout is clean. Several Dedicated customers run with tight latency SLOs + bursty queues, so I’d rather have us explicitly coordinate pool by pool.

I’m good with the success metrics you proposed, but I’d like to add a single “customer-visible” KPI for decision-making:
- p99 end-to-end (not just decode) on the mixed-length burst scenario in perf canary, because that’s what we’re getting escalations on.

If we want to share an improvement story later, we should capture “before/after” with a concrete scenario and baseline commit SHA.

Thanks,
Nikhil

Nikhil Sharma
Product, Hosted API — Redwood Inference

2) Send a weekly status (2-3 bullets) starting next week: current fragmentation metrics, canary status, risks.

If there’s any realistic chance of slipping runtime-1.22, flag early — I’d rather we reduce scope than ship without guardrails/kill-switch.

Ava

Aligned. Summary of decisions / next steps:

Decisions
- Priority: KV compaction/eviction is runtime-1.22 P0.
- Rollout order: internal perf canary -> Hosted 1% canary w/ auto rollback -> Hosted ramp -> Dedicated opt-in pool-by-pool.
- Kill-switch authority: SRE oncall can disable immediately for Hosted; runtime-oncall notified.

Gating criteria to document (I’ll put these in Confluence today)
- p99 end-to-end latency: hold canary to <= 1.20x baseline for 10 min; spike threshold <= 1.35x for 3 min.
- Error/OOM: no increase; explicit OOM threshold in canary to be tuned w/ SRE after day 1.
- Compaction overhead: budgeted and observable; “overrun” triggers rollback.

Actions
- I’ll update the design doc with gating criteria + rollback thresholds and link the release plan ticket.
- Sean: please confirm the initial alert wiring owner + where the canary dashboards will live.
- Nikhil: we’ll treat Hosted as silent + Dedicated as opt-in until Hosted is clean.

Links
- Design doc (WIP, will be updated with gating): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SERVE/KV+cache+compaction+improvements+(Design+Doc)
- Linear epic: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/kv-cache-compaction-epic
- Release plan stub: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4829/runtime-release-plan-runtime-1-22

I’ll start weekly status next week.
